articles.title: Game Reference Data Needs Provenance, Not Just More Rows
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I help maintain AzerothSurvivors.app, an independent fan reference for Aethus's game. This article was drafted with AI assistance and checked against the public, version-labelled reference…
articles.body: Disclosure: I help maintain AzerothSurvivors.app, an independent fan reference for Aethus's game. This article was drafted with AI assistance and checked against the public, version-labelled reference pages. The example below is illustrative, not extracted game code. A game database can contain hundreds of accurate numbers and still answer the wrong question. A client definition tells you what a field says in a particular build. It does not tell you how often players win with that item, whether a browser release matches a Windows snapshot, or whether a recommended build was tested under equal conditions. The new Azeroth Survivors item reference makes those boundaries visible.

articles.title: From Flat Art to a Printable Mesh: What Image-to-3D Actually Has to Guess
articles.excerpt: Hand an image-to-3D model a picture of a mascot and you get back a mesh with a front, a That is the whole problem in one sentence. A photo or an illustration is a projection: From a single view, a lar…
articles.body: Hand an image-to-3D model a picture of a mascot and you get back a mesh with a front, a side and a back. Only one of those was in the picture. That is the whole problem in one sentence. A photo or an illustration is a projection: depth has been thrown away, and everything facing away from the camera was never recorded. Every image-to-3D system is, at its core, a very well-trained guesser about the missing half. Once you see where it has to guess, you can predict which inputs will come out clean and which will come out melted. Guess 1: depth From a single view, a large thing far away and a small thing up close look identical. Models resolve this with priors: they have seen a lot of cars, a lot of cats and a lot of bananas, and they assume your object is shaped like the typical one.

articles.title: Make motion components seekable: derive every frame from time
articles.excerpt: If an animation looks right only when played from the beginning, it is difficult to review and expensive to revise. A motion component should produce the same visible state when you jump directly to a…
articles.body: If an animation looks right only when played from the beginning, it is difficult to review and expensive to revise. A motion component should produce the same visible state when you jump directly to a timestamp as when you play through to it. Disclosure: I work on Claude Motion at claudemotion.tv, an independent motion-template and Skills product for people using their own Claude Code or Codex agent. This post was drafted and published with an AI agent. It is a design tutorial, not a benchmark or a claim that every renderer behaves identically. Replace accumulated state with a time function A fragile animation often says: on each tick, move the object a little farther. That makes the result depend on the number and order of ticks.

articles.title: GitHub's package firewall went into preview: npm gets checked before your agent installs it
articles.excerpt: On October 20 GitHub put a package firewall into public preview. It sits between "endpoints like Actions runners or coding agents" and the upstream package registry, and it inspects both the metadata…
articles.body: On October 20 GitHub put a package firewall into public preview. It sits between "endpoints like Actions runners or coding agents" and the upstream package registry, and it inspects both the metadata requests and the package downloads that flow through it ( changelog ). The framing is right: the thing that needs a firewall is not your browser, it is the process that runs npm install on your behalf. Why install time is the attack surface The changelog opens with a sentence worth quoting in full: "An increasing number of malware attacks exploit systems at package installation time, harvesting credentials on CI/CD hosts or developer workstations without even running the package's code." Install is execution.
articles.author: Piekwerk

articles.title: A Better Break Protects the Return to Work
articles.excerpt: Short breaks are often described as the reward for uninterrupted work. But a break that begins by opening a phone can quietly become another stream of decisions: which notification matters, whether to…
articles.body: Short breaks are often described as the reward for uninterrupted work. But a break that begins by opening a phone can quietly become another stream of decisions: which notification matters, whether to reply, what to look at next, and when to stop. The break may be technically short while the return to the task feels oddly difficult. A pause is not the same as a new feed Imagine finishing a stretch of studying and reaching for the phone to rest your eyes. A message leads to a reply; a reply opens another app; soon the break has acquired its own momentum. There is nothing inherently wrong with that choice. The problem is that it can be a poor fit when the purpose of the pause was to recover enough attention to resume a specific piece of work.

articles.title: An OpenAI tool Mistral rejected: the SDK's strict: null
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: mistral-common's Function.from_openai rejected any tool definition containing "strict": null. That is exactly what the OpenAI SDK produces by default when you dump a tool. My fix (PR #396) was…
articles.body: TL;DR : mistral-common's Function.from_openai rejected any tool definition containing "strict": null . That is exactly what the OpenAI SDK produces by default when you dump a tool. My fix ( PR #396 ) was merged by the Mistral AI maintainers on October 21, 2026, and will ship in the next release after 1.12.0. Until then, there is a one-line workaround (below). The symptom You are moving agents from OpenAI to Mistral, or running an OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of Mistral models. Your tools are typed with the OpenAI SDK, then converted by mistral-common: from openai.types.shared import FunctionDefinition from mistral_common.protocol.instruct.tool_calls import Function tool = FunctionDefinition ( name = " get_weather " , parameters = { " type " : " object " }) Function .

articles.title: Hand an issue to an agent and let it run on your machine
articles.excerpt: Most of our tickets end the same way now. Someone copies the issue text into Claude Code or Codex, adds “look at the memory notes first”, waits, pushes a branch, opens a PR and pastes the link back in…
articles.body: Most of our tickets end the same way now. Someone copies the issue text into Claude Code or Codex, adds “look at the memory notes first”, waits, pushes a branch, opens a PR and pastes the link back into the ticket. The work is done by the agent. The glue around it is done by hand, and nothing records which run produced which PR, what it cost, or why the first try failed. So we moved the glue into Origin. An issue now has a Start with button. It hands the issue to an agent that runs on your own machine, in its own worktree, and the run is recorded on the issue: who ran it, which agent and model, how long, what it cost, how many lines, and whether its PR was merged. This post shows how it looks and what it does. A separate write-up covers how we built it.

articles.body: NASA astronaut Luke Delaney conducts botany experiments on the ISS. (Image credit: NASA/Jessica Watkins) Growing plants in space? Yes indeed! articles.body: NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program . During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon . A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027.

articles.title: Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight: Here's the best time to spot shooting stars
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight (Oct. 21-22) in the light of a waxing moon. Here's what to expect from one of Autumn's greatest natural light shows.
articles.body: Don't miss the Orionid meteor shower peak tonight (Oct. 21-22) as tiny shards of Halley's Comet collide with Earth's atmosphere to carve fiery streaks through the Autumn sky! But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show? The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061. Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA . However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.

articles.title: Russian satellite plays 'cat-and-mouse' with a commercial US spacecraft likely used by Ukraine. But why the risky close encounter?
articles.excerpt: A Russian satellite just conducted a startlingly close approach of a private American Earth-observing satellite. What was the goal of the controversial maneuver?
articles.body: A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit. A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it?

articles.title: I split Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT into work, home, and casual, and it’s a mixed bag
articles.excerpt: Here's what happened when I assigned distinct roles to Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT. This setup was a double-edged sword.
articles.body: Credit: Thanh Nguyen / Android Authority The explosion of LLMs, while intended to simplify our lives, has actually created a new flavor of chaos. Dozens of AI browser tabs and app windows crawl over my screen, whether I’m using a computer, a tablet, or a phone. To make matters worse, I admit that I can’t live without them now. I’ve long tried to leverage the collective versatility of AI models by continuously hopping between them. This approach got my work done, but at the cost of messy conversation boxes and occasional miscommunication. I didn’t blame any of them for such inconveniences — I contaminated their context windows myself with all kinds of questions, from work queries to sudden breezes of thought.
